title: Styled-under-shipped-CSP adherence probe refuses ship on inline styles or unstyled runtime
asA: operator relying on the security baseline the application-spa blueprint declares
iWant: a runtime check that fails the build when the application ships with inline style blocks, a CSP relaxed to unsafe-inline, or a runtime surface that renders unstyled under the shipped headers
soThat: the application-spa-REQ-018 security floor is enforced at the ship gate and every UI surface reaches production styled without the CSP being weakened

acceptanceCriteria.description: The CSP served on every HTML document declares style-src that resolves to 'self' (or a nonce / hash allowlist), and NEVER contains the 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' relaxations. A wildcard style-src is refused; declaring 'unsafe-inline' as a fallback is refused. The CSP style-src is the sole styling-authority signal the runtime respects; a stylesheet the CSP would refuse is a defect, not a warning.
acceptanceCriteria.then: style-src is present, resolves to 'self' or a nonce / hash allowlist, and contains neither 'unsafe-inline' nor 'unsafe-eval' nor a wildcard source

acceptanceCriteria.description: No HTML surface shipped by the application carries an inline <style> block. Stylesheets are served from same-origin routes referenced via <link rel="stylesheet">; every occurrence of <style> in a rendered response body is a defect, including <style> injected via templating helpers or partials.
acceptanceCriteria.given: any rendered HTML response from the application surface
acceptanceCriteria.when: the response body is scanned for the substring '<style'
acceptanceCriteria.then: zero occurrences are present; a positive match is a hard refusal

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every UI-bearing route renders styled UNDER the shipped strict CSP, AND the probe proves it exercised the requested surface (not a page a redirect would land on). A browser-driven check drives the same server instance that stamps the production security headers, navigates each enumerated UI route, and asserts (a) the browser's final URL path equals the requested route path; a silent redirect (for example an authenticated route 302'ing to /login when the harness session is broken) is a hard refusal because a headless browser follows redirects by default and would otherwise validate the redirect target's styled state seven times over, and (b) the computed body background is NOT the browser default (rgba(0,0,0,0) / transparent) and the computed body font-family resolves to a non-empty value. Verification runs through the production header path; a harness that strips the security headers, injects nonces the CSP does not declare, or invokes the app via app.inject() rather than a real browser fetch does NOT satisfy the AC. Cures the class of harness where a broken session lane silently causes every route assertion to run against /login (styled) and pass (watchpost run4 partial-acceptance gap, w-2026-08-24-003 / AC-1601-14).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a server booted through the project's production entry point with every UI-bearing route registered
acceptanceCriteria.when: a real browser navigates each enumerated route, its final URL is read, and getComputedStyle(document.body) is read
acceptanceCriteria.then: the final URL path equals the requested route (no silent redirect chain to another surface) AND the computed background is not the browser default AND the computed font-family resolves; on any route the check fails, the run refuses ship with a per-route diagnostic naming the requested and landed paths

acceptanceCriteria.description: The stylesheet-serving route is registered by the same server construction that stamps the production security headers. A separate server instance, a static-file-only mount, or a build harness that skips the shipped header stack does NOT satisfy the AC. The intent is that a same-origin GET for the linked stylesheet URL returns 200 with content-type text/css under the same headers a browser sees for the HTML documents.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the application boot topology at ship
acceptanceCriteria.when: the boot topology is inspected AND a same-origin GET is issued for the URL every rendered HTML links via <link rel="stylesheet">
acceptanceCriteria.then: the stylesheet is served by the same server instance that stamps the production headers AND the response is 200 with content-type text/css

acceptanceCriteria.description: The styled-under-shipped-CSP adherence probe (TAC-209) writes a JSON report at a stable relative path (`reports/csp-styled-adherence.json` under the configured report directory) naming every route probed, the CSP header captured for that route, whether an inline <style> was detected, the computed body background and font-family, the landed URL path (the browser's final URL after any redirect chain resolved) so a pathMismatch refusal names both the requested and landed paths, and an ok / fail verdict.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a completed probe run (pass or fail)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the report file is inspected on disk
acceptanceCriteria.then: the JSON at `reports/csp-styled-adherence.json` matches the shape declared by TAC-209 and its verdict field agrees with the process exit code

acceptanceCriteria.description: When the styled-under-shipped-CSP adherence probe is wired as a gate in the ci-pipeline runner (TAC-701), a non-zero probe exit propagates through the per-gate report (TAC-702) and the aggregate report (TAC-703), and the ci-pipeline runner refuses ship with a non-zero exit.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the ci-pipeline runner configured with the styled-under-CSP adherence probe as a required gate
acceptanceCriteria.when: the probe reports `fail` on any run
acceptanceCriteria.then: the aggregate report records the gate as failed and the runner exits non-zero
